meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so you have twenty minutes. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Now the basis, Hale. What do you have?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
A misquote. Students get Shakespeare wrong every day, and that costs marks, not the whole essay. Did anyone ask Owen where that line came from before the zero went in?
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
You'll want to be very careful about your next sentence, Hale. "It seems to run in the family." I'm writing that down, and it goes to the principal today, along with the zero.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero on Owen's Hamlet essay to be withdrawn, a written apology, and nothing placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, she agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the principal involved today.
What moved her: "I should have called you before entering the zero", because owning the process in one sentence earned a flat okay and she started asking real questions.
What cost ground: "It seems to run in the family", because bringing up Claire turned an evidence discussion into an attack on her family and sent her to the principal.
Try next time: after the misquoted line got her asking where it came from, answer that question with something dated from Owen's own process or other samples of his work instead of raising Claire.
